title: Do different masses fall together?
question: Do a light ball and a heavy ball take different times to reach the ground?
steps: Put both balls at the same height.
Change the gravity to the Moon or Jupiter.
Compare when the two balls reach the ground.
observe: See how the gravity of the place, more than the mass, changes how the falling speed grows.

terms.name: Mass
terms.description: How much a thing resists a change in its motion.

terms.name: Gravity
terms.description: The force with which a body like the Earth pulls things towards it.

terms.name: Acceleration
terms.description: How quickly the speed changes over time.

law.title: Gravity and acceleration
law.description: Gravity pulls things down and keeps changing their speed.

tip: Drag a ball up or down with one finger to set the height (1 m steps) and let go: both balls fall together. Drag again to start over. Drag with two fingers to turn the view.
tip_short: Drag a ball and let go: both balls fall

predict.question: Will the heavy ball land first?
predict.reason: Heavy and light balls speed up at the same rate. So dropped from the same height, they land together.
predict.bridge: Drop them and see for yourself!

stages.text: Drop the red and pink balls together to press the buttons!
stages.say: The pull of the ground is called gravity. Gravity makes heavy and light balls speed up at the same rate. So dropped from the same height, they land together.
stages.win: Click! Both buttons went down together!
stages.miss: The balls landed apart. Make them the same height!

stages.text: On the Moon, drop both balls together from the very top!
stages.say: The Moon's gravity is weaker than the Earth's, so it pulls gently. That is why the balls fall slowly. From the very top it takes more than 3 seconds.
stages.win: Together on the Moon too! The light is on!
stages.miss: Take the pink ball up to the top like the red one!

stages.text: On Jupiter, drop both balls together in under 1 second!
stages.say: Jupiter's gravity is much stronger than the Earth's. So the balls fall very fast. But the two balls still land together.
stages.win: The door opened! I see the piece!
stages.miss: On Jupiter, put both balls at the same height!

story.clue: The piece is locked in the blue house! I think the door opens if we press both buttons together!
story.map_clue: Something twinkled on top of the blue tower!

kid.intro: This is the ball drop lab. The ground pulls everything down. This pull is called gravity. Let's see how a heavy ball and a light ball fall!
kid.title: Let's drop balls from up high!
kid.say: A heavy ball and a light ball fall the same way. Dropped from the same height, they land together. They fall slowly on the Moon and fast on Jupiter.
kid.tip: Drag a ball up and let go: both balls fall together!

note.law: Dropped from the same height, a heavy ball and a light ball fall together. The smaller the gravity g, the longer it takes.
